title: PowerDisplay doesn't find my monitor (KVM switch)

status.label: KVM/DDC path needs confirmation
status.detail: PowerDisplay does not find the reporter’s monitor through a KVM switch.

next_action.label: Confirm the monitor control path through the KVM.
next_action.reason: Review the discovery-status proposal after confirming the KVM path.

judgment.rationale: Distinguish a Windows-enumerated monitor from one whose DDC/CI handle is unavailable; do not promise control if the KVM blocks that channel.
judgment.recommended_action: Review the discovery-status proposal after confirming the KVM path.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current discovery uses DDC/CI physical handles and skips monitors without a stable DevicePath; the KVM-specific report makes the distinction between OS enumeration and control-channel availability useful, but the KVM behavior is unconfirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Explain when a Windows-visible monitor has no usable DDC/CI path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The KVM may leave the display visible to Windows while preventing PowerDisplay from obtaining a usable physical-monitor handle; this is a hypothesis.
plan: Reproduce with the display directly connected and through the KVM.
Trace Windows enumeration separately from physical-handle and DevicePath availability.
If currently conflated, show a specific unavailable-control reason without claiming that the monitor can be controlled.
verification: Verify direct-connect and KVM cases report distinct discovery/control states.
Verify DDC/CI-capable displays retain their controls.

confidence.rationale: The DDC path and KVM relationship are source-grounded, but the KVM’s behavior is unconfirmed.

issue_context.summary: PowerDisplay does not find the reporter’s monitor through a KVM switch.
known_information: The report explicitly identifies a KVM switch and says the monitor is not found by PowerDisplay.
Current DDC discovery needs a usable physical-monitor handle and stable Windows DevicePath; a KVM may pass display output but block DDC/CI.
inferences: KVM DDC/CI forwarding is a plausible cause, but direct-connect behavior and Windows enumeration are not established.
issue_context.analysis: Distinguish a Windows-enumerated monitor from one whose DDC/CI handle is unavailable; do not promise control if the KVM blocks that channel.

information_gaps.information: Whether Windows lists the monitor model, the KVM make/model, and whether PowerDisplay finds it when connected directly without the KVM.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates Windows enumeration from KVM DDC/CI forwarding and shows whether a PowerToys fix can help.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please check the monitor name in Windows Settings > System > Display, share the KVM model, and, if convenient, report whether PowerDisplay lists the monitor connected directly.

actions.label: Check monitor discovery through the KVM

comment.body: Thanks for identifying the KVM. PowerDisplay’s external-monitor path needs a usable DDC/CI handle; a KVM can pass the picture while not forwarding that control channel. Could you share the KVM make/model and confirm whether Windows lists the monitor by model name? If practical, does PowerDisplay list it when connected directly without the KVM? This distinguishes a discovery defect from a control protocol the KVM does not expose; no additional files are needed.
